actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository provides a MuJoCo simulation stack for Stretch with position control for the arm, head and gripper joints, velocity control for the mobile base, RGB and depth camera imagery and 2D lidar scans
The StretchMujocoSimulator class is documented to start the simulation, position-control the robot's ranged joints, velocity-control its mobile base, and read joint states and camera imagery
The upstream default scene is models/scene.xml and the default robot model is models/stretch.xml
The upstream URDF model name defaults to SE3
The simulator loads the scene MJCF with MjModel.from_xml_path(scene_xml_path) and creates the MjData from that model
The upstream reads every joint's range from mjmodel.jnt_range for njnt joints and records it as a joint limit
The upstream writes a move_to command to data.actuator(name).ctrl and a keyframe command to mjmodel.keyframe(name).ctrl
The scene includes stretch.xml and docking_station.xml
The Stretch body is a free base: base_link carries <freejoint/>
The actuator defaults set the wheel control range to -6 to 6 and the lift control range to 0 to 1.1
The actuator defaults set the telescope control range to 0 to 0.52, head_pan to -4.04 to 1.73 and head_tilt to -1.53 to 0.79
The actuator defaults set wrist_yaw to -1.39 to 4.42, wrist_pitch to -1.57 to 0.56, wrist_roll to -3.14 to 3.14 and the gripper slide to -0.02 to 0.04
The actuator block declares ten actuators: two velocity actuators for the wheels and eight position actuators for lift, arm, wrist_yaw, wrist_pitch, wrist_roll, gripper, head_pan and head_tilt
The arm position actuator drives the fixed tendon extend, which sums the four arm slide joints joint_arm_l0, joint_arm_l1, joint_arm_l2 and joint_arm_l3
The robot declares two wheel hinge joints, a lift slide joint and four arm telescope slide joints
The head declares pan and tilt hinge joints and a nav-camera hinge joint
The model declares the cameras d405_rgb and d405_depth, d435i_camera_rgb and d435i_camera_depth, and nav_camera_rgb
The model declares a gyro, an accelerometer and a rangefinder lidar sensor on base_imu and lidar sites
The model declares home and stow keyframes, each with a ten-element ctrl vector
The model sets no option timestep: its option element carries integrator implicitfast, impratio 20 and cone elliptic
A second Stretch robot model, stretch_mj_3.3.0.xml, declares the same ten actuators
The docking station is a free body: link_docking_station carries <freejoint/>

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the served model has no random element, so one ctrl sequence and tick count repeat a trajectory; the bridge takes no seed input and a reset restores the model defaults, so no seed selects a different one. The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics and it offers no snapshot state.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the served scene.xml with its includes, takes the ten actuator control ranges, the joint dimensions and the option time step from the tree, then moves each actuated joint toward its control value; it computes no inertia, torque, contact, equality, tendon or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result

the stand-in loads no mesh or texture and resolves no contact: the scene's table, free objects and docking station are not simulated physically, and the arm equality and tendon constraints only distribute a control target in the placeholder
the model states no option timestep (stretch.xml:7-9); the stand-in uses a placeholder library default, and the bridge publishes that stand-in value from the stand-in
the stand-in does not apply the model's gear, gain, bias, damping, friction, armature or force ranges, and a wheel velocity actuator is treated as a direct joint velocity target
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine

no rendering, cameras, lidar scans or gripper range mapping are published: the upstream StretchMujocoSimulator camera, sensor and joint-status API (README.md:101-107) is not part of this driver, which exposes only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state
the card's other robot model, stretch_mj_3.3.0.xml, is not served: one package serves one device, and the driver and fake use models[0], the default scene
no physical Stretch is modelled and nothing was validated against the hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
